Nothing asks what order an increment can be built in, and budget.rs hand-rolls the algorithm that would answer it

*Found 2026-08-01 by a review of what dynograph-foundation v0.12.0 offers that reflow2 does not use, at Anthony's request. The headline number: reflow2 consumes 8 of 17 dynograph-graph exports, 2 of ~35 dynograph-vector functions, and none of dynograph-game — there is more unused foundation than used. The full option set, including the ideas NOT filed, is recorded as proposed Decisions (dec:idea-*) so the roads not taken stay in the design's memory.* Two findings, one function. (1) A simplification available today: budget.rs:312 implements Kahn's algorithm in about forty lines under a comment that says *"Kahn's toposort; leftovers mean a cycle"* — while dynograph_graph::topological_sort is exported, is Kahn's, is deterministic (the lexicographically-smallest valid order, so it is stable run to run) and returns None on a cycle. It was reimplemented because nobody knew it was there, which is itself the finding. (2) A capability that does not exist: capabilities form a DEPENDS_ON DAG that detect_defects insists stays acyclic, and nothing ever asks what order that DAG implies. reflow2 can say what is scheduled for an increment (SCHEDULED_FOR) and what has been delivered (the golden thread), but not *what can be started now*. Lands on [BL-68] (TRL/MRL readiness gating): that item asks whether a thing is ready, this asks whether its DEPENDENCIES are — the other half of the same question — and on epoch planning generally. THE SHAPE IS OPEN (dec:idea-build-order), and the objection is real: a topological order is ONE valid order among many, and presenting it as THE order would assert a schedule reflow2 has no business asserting — the overreach dec:report-dont-judge exists to prevent. The honest output is probably the READY FRONTIER (what currently has no unbuilt dependency) rather than a full ordering. Note also that (1) is not free: the local version works on string-id arcs while the foundation one wants a Graph built through GraphBuilder, so it trades forty tested lines for an adapter. Size S for (1), M for (2)

Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-150 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S–M.
